{{Quote|Draven was on to something. At Scarif, however, these soldiers weren't assigned. They volunteered for an unsanctioned mission.|Caluan Ematt on Timker and the other rebels recommended by Draven, ''The Rebel Files''|<ref name="RebelFiles">''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]''</ref>}}
'''Walea Timker''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|female]] who served as a combat [[engineer]] and [[corporal]] for the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] and was based in the [[Great Temple]] on the [[moon]] [[Yavin 4]]. In [[1 BBY]], [[General]] [[Davits Draven]] recommended her to Alliance leader [[Mon Mothma]] as a potential candidate for a strike team to raid the [[Catacombs of Cadera|stronghold]] of [[Partisans|partisan]] [[Saw Gerrera]] on the moon [[Jedha]], although the raid ultimately did not happen as the criminal [[Jyn Erso]] successfully made contact with Gerrera for the Alliance.

After Erso later led an unsanctioned [[Battle of Scarif|mission]] to the [[planet]] [[Scarif]] to steal the [[Death Star plans|plans]] to the [[Galactic Empire]]'s [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[superweapon]], Timker volunteered to join rebel forces that traveled to the [[Scarif system]] to aid Erso and her [[Rogue One|team]]. Timker traveled to Scarif in a [[Blue Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Blue Squadron]] [[UT-60D U-wing starfighter/support craft]] that dropped the combat engineer off on one of the world's beaches. Timker [[Death|died]] during the assault against the Imperials, but her sacrifice helped buy Erso enough [[time]] to successfully steal the plans.

==Biography==
===Strike team potential===
{{Quote|Most of these are bios you've seen before. It takes genuine fearlessness (or foolishness) to rush in against long odds, but those who also possess self-awareness stand a chance of remaining alive past the first minute. I recommend we begin with these soldiers and build a larger squad around them.|General Davits Draven on Timker and his ten other recommendations in a communication to Mon Mothma|<ref name="RebelFiles" />}}
[[File:StrikeTeamSuggestions-RF.png|thumb|right|300px|Davits Draven recommended Walea Timker as part of a potential Jedha strike team.]]
Walea Timker was a [[human]]<ref name="UVG" /> [[Gender|female]] who served in the [[Rebel Alliance Special Forces|Special Forces]] of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]]<ref name="Geektionary" /> as a [[combat engineer]], specialising in finding, improvising, and constructing temporary fortifications across a battlefield<ref name="UVG" /> during military operations.<ref name="Geektionary" /> A part of the [[Massassi Group]] of rebels, she was based out of the [[Great Temple]] on the [[moon]] [[Yavin 4]] and had earned the rank of [[corporal]]<ref name="UVG" /> by [[1 BBY]].<ref name="Date" />

In that [[Standard year|year]],<ref name="Date" /> the Alliance sent the criminal [[Jyn Erso]] to make contact with the [[Partisans|partisan]] leader [[Saw Gerrera]] in his [[Catacombs of Cadera|stronghold]] on the moon [[Jedha]] to try and [[Operation Fracture|learn the location]] of her [[Parent|father]], the [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] [[scientist]] [[Galen Walton Erso|Galen Erso]], from [[Bodhi Rook]], an Imperial defector that Gerrera held [[prisoner]].<ref name="Rogue One">''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''</ref> As a backup contingency for if Jyn should fail, [[General]] [[Davits Draven]] of [[Rebel Alliance Intelligence Service|Alliance Intelligence]] put together a list of eleven rebel [[soldier]]s, including Timker, around whom a rapid response strike team could be built for a raid on Gerrera's fortress. He sent the soldier's bios to to [[Mon Mothma]], leader of the Alliance, in an intelligence update about the team, although Mothma had seen all of the bios before.<ref name="RebelFiles" />

===Unsanctioned volunteer===
The team was ultimately unneeded,<ref name="RebelFiles" /> as Jyn made contact with Gerrera and then managed to locate her father, learning about a weakness that could be used to destroy the Empire's [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[superweapon]] should the [[Death Star plans|plans]] for the [[battle station]] be recovered. Jyn brough this information back to Yavin and proposed that the Alliance strike the [[Citadel Tower|Imperial facility]] on the [[planet]] [[Scarif]] where the [[Death Star]] plans were stored, but the idea was rejected by the [[Alliance Cabinet|Alliance's leadership]]. Determined to steal the plans anyway, Jyn gathered a [[Rogue One|group]] of rebel volunteers to travel with her on an unsanctioned [[Battle of Scarif|mission]] to Scarif and Timker ran past her and the Intelligence [[agent]] [[Cassian Jeron Andor|Cassian Andor]] in one of the Great Temple's [[hangar]]s as the pair prepared to depart.<ref name="Rogue One" />

Once fighting broke out between Jyn's team and the Imperials on Scarif, word got back to Yavin about the mission and the [[Rebel Alliance Navy|Alliance fleet]] was scrambled to travel to the [[Scarif system]] and support them.<ref name="Rogue One" /> Timker and the other two remaining recommendations from Draven's list, [[Bistan]] and [[Rodma Maddel]], volunteered<ref name="RebelFiles" /> to join the forces travelling to Scarif with Timker and Maddel making up part of the ground reinforcements that would be deployed to the planet's surface to support Jyn and her team.<ref name="UVG" />

The trio then traveled to Scarif in the [[UT-60D U-wing starfighter/support craft]] [[pilot]]ed by [[Laren Joma]] and [[Taslet Colb]] of [[Blue Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Blue Squadron]].<ref name="Geektionary" /> Upon reaching the Scarif system, Blue Squadron almost immediatly raced for the planet's surface in order to make it through a closing Imperial [[Shield Gate]] that was the only route through Scarif's [[planetary shield]].<ref name="Rogue One" /> The [[Starship|ship]] carrying Timker was the only U-wing to make it through the gate before it closed,<ref name="HC71">{{HelmetCollectionCite|71|Weapons & Uniforms}}</ref> although a number of the [[squadron]]'s [[T-65 X-wing starfighter]]s also reached the surface.<ref name="Rogue One" />

===Fight them on the beaches===
{{Quote|For Jedha!|The ground reinforcements on Scarif|<ref name="Rogue One" />}}
After the U-wing and [[X-wing starfighter|X-wings]] that had made it through destroyed several Imperial [[All Terrain Armored Cargo Transport]]s from the air, General [[Antoc Merrick]], [[Blue Leader|leader]] of Blue Squadron, ordered Joma to drop off Timker and the other reinforcements on a beach near Jyn's forces while the X-wings protected the U-wing. Joma and Colb brought the ship down to hover just above the beach so that Timker and the other [[Trooper|troops]] could disembark. As the passengers did so, some gave a battle cry in memory of Jedha, which had [[Destruction of Jedha City|sustained great damage]] from the Death Star's [[superlaser]].<ref name="Rogue One" />

Although only a fairly modest reinforcement, Timker and the others who arrived with her provided a much needed second wind to those already fighting on Jedha due to the losses they had suffered.<ref name="Geektionary" /> Given the wreckage the rebels on Scarif had already caused before she arrived, Timker had plenty of structures to chose from for the fortifications<ref name="UVG" /> she used to protect her comrades.<ref name="Heroes">{{EncyclopediaCite|The Heroes of Rogue One}}</ref> Timker [[Death|died]] during the assault against the Imperials, but her sacrifice was not in vain, as she and the other rebels on the beaches managed to buy enough [[time]] for Jyn and Andor to steal the Death Star plans<ref name="Geektionary" /> and transmit them to the rebel [[fleet]] above before the Death Star fired upon Scarif, obliterating the area where Timker had fallen and killing all those still there, including Andor and Jyn.<ref name="Rogue One" /> The plans then allowed the Alliance to destroy the Death Star at the [[Battle of Yavin]].<ref name="Atlas">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]''</ref>

===Legacy===
Dravens communication to Mothma mentioning Timker was included in the collection of rebel documentation known as ''[[The Rebel Files]]'' where, after the files were obtained by the [[Resistance]]<ref name="RebelFiles" /> in [[34 ABY]],<ref name="FilesDate">''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]'' states that ''[[The Rebel Files]]'' were sent to the [[Resistance]] thirty [[Standard year|years]] after the [[Battle of Endor]]. As ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the battle to [[4 ABY]], the files must have been received in [[34 ABY]].</ref> Reistance [[Lieutenant]] [[Caluan Ematt]], formerly a member of the Alliance, added a note complimenting Draven's choices and mentioning how Timker and the others volunteered for Scarif.<ref name="RebelFiles" />

==Personality and traits==
Timker was an exceptionally skilled battlefield veteran who was accustomed to encountering the unexpected during military campaigns.<ref name="Topps" /> She was inspired by the unsanctioned efforts of those that had gone to Scarif<ref name="HC62">{{HelmetCollectionCite|62|Weapons & Uniforms}}</ref> and was greatly pleased to take part in the mission to Scarif, as it would lead to the demise of the Death Star.<ref name="Topps" /> Draven considered all of the candidates he picked for his potential strike team as either fearless or foolish enough to rush in against long odds, but also believed they possessed enough self-awareness to survive longer then the first [[Standard minute|minute]] of the mission.<ref name="RebelFiles" /> The corporal had light skin, [[Color|brown]] [[hair]], and gray [[eye]]s.<ref name="Topps" />

==Equipment==
While on Yavin,<ref name="Rogue One" /> Timker wore a light brown [[jacket]] over a black [[Clothing|shirt]] with a dark brown [[scarf]] and black pants. She had a brown [[utility belt]] with carriage loops and carried a black [[blaster]].<ref name="UVG" />

==Behind the scenes==
Walea Timker was created for the [[2016]] [[Star Wars Anthology Series|Anthology Series]] film, ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'',<ref name="Rogue One" /> and was first identified in the accompanying reference book ''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'', which was written by [[Pablo Hidalgo]].<ref name="UVG" />
